You\’ve probably heard about companies like Google and Facebook tracking you behind the scenes on third-party websites. But did you know they also track your personal information through apps on your device? Over 96\% of the 100 popular free Android apps we tested contained hidden third-party trackers. Of those, 87\% sent data to Google and 68\% sent data to Facebook. This happens even when you\’re not using your device. Trackers in apps may have access to a lot more information than their website tracker cousins, such as your location down to which floor of a building you're on, how often you play games while at work, and when and how long you sleep each day. Even if you don't have a Google or Facebook account, for example, they can still collect data about you from your apps. Tracking networks like Facebook and Google use these little pieces of information to build a digital profile about you. With it, tracking networks can manipulate what you see online and allow advertisers to bid on access to you based on your data. Trackers in apps is a BIG problem for privacy. But DuckDuckGo has a solution that can help. When enabled in the DuckDuckGo Privacy Browser app, App Tracking Protection blocks many trackers in other apps on your device, at the same time that the DuckDuckGo app blocks trackers we find on websites when you browse. These dual layers of protection reduce what tracking companies know about you overall, so you can use your apps with more peace of mind, knowing you\’re more protected.

You’ll be asked to set up a virtual private network (VPN) connection, but you don't need to install a VPN app for App Tracking Protection to work.\n\nThis permission allows App Tracking Protection, which works locally on your device, to monitor network traffic so that it can block known trackers.

Android only allows one active VPN connection at a time. That means you can\’t use App Tracking Protection while a VPN app on your device is running or set to “Always on.”\n\nWe recommend that you enable App Tracking Protection when you are not using a VPN app Just make sure your VPN app isn’t set to "always-on". Go to Android Network settings > VPN. Then, check the gear icon for any listed VPN apps and disable"always-on." Some VPN apps may also have an auto-connect setting which must be disabled.

A VPN sends your data from the device to its own server, where it secures and anonymizes your data from prying eyes. However, this allows the VPN company to see your network traffic. App Tracking Protection is different. Instead of sending your data to a VPN server, App Tracking Protection works locally on your device, sitting between your apps and the servers they talk to. Whenever App Tracking Protection recognizes a known tracker, it blocks the tracker from sending personal information (such as your IP address, activity, and device details) off your device. All other traffic reaches its destination, so your apps work normally.
App Tracking Protection works on your device and doesn’t send your personal data off your device to DuckDuckGo.

How does DuckDuckGo VPN work?

The VPN uses the open source WireGuard protocol to configure a virtual private network (VPN) on your device. When enabled, all of your device traffic is first encrypted and then routed through the nearest VPN server to protect your browsing activity from Internet service providers and hide your location from apps and sites you visit.
Is only my web browsing protected?
All of the network activity on your device is protected.
Does DuckDuckGo keep logs of my data?
No, we do not store logs.
Where are the VPN servers located?
DuckDuckGo offers a limited number of servers while DuckDuckGo VPN is in beta, located in the United States, Canada, and Europe.
Why do some apps not work when the VPN is on?

Some websites and apps intentionally limit access to people using a VPN. For example, they may ask you to solve a CAPTCHA to ensure you're a real person instead of a bot. If you experience repeated issues with an app, you can exclude it from the VPN altogether under DuckDuckGo VPN settings.
Why can't I dismiss VPN notifications?
Android requires that VPNs show a persistent notification while the VPN is enabled.
Is the VPN compatible with App Tracking Protection?
Yes, both the VPN and App Tracking Protection can be on at the same time. No other VPNs are compatible with DuckDuckGo App Tracking Protection.
Is the VPN free to use?
DuckDuckGo VPN is free to use while in beta. Eventually it will be offered as a paid service.
